 One control center for Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and other coding agents. 
 Run agents locally or on a VPS, automate multi-step workflows, 
 and let them keep working while you're away.
 
 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 
 ▶ Watch the video: Meet cezar, your new parallel coding tool. 
 

 Features

- 💯 Free and open source.
- 🖥️ Uses your own claude , codex , copilot , cursor , agy (Antigravity), gemini , junie , kimi (Kimi Code), omp , opencode or pi login. No API key needed.
- ☁️ Easy to set up on a VPS, so your agents keep working when your laptop is closed.
- 📱 Fully responsive. Start and review tasks from your phone.
- 🔀 Every task gets its own git worktree, so several agents can work at the same time. Extra tasks wait in a queue.
- 🤖 Turn on Autonomous and a run never stops to ask. It just finishes.
- 📡 Watch it work live: agent text, tool calls, tokens and cost.
- 🏁 Run the same task ×2 or ×3, compare the diffs and keep the best one.
- 🧩 Skills are Markdown files and workflows are short YAML files. Mix agents per step.
- 🐙 Run the agent straight on a GitHub issue. Nothing merges on its own.
- 📂 One cockpit for all your projects.
- 📊 A workspace dashboard shows what needs you, what is running and what finished across your projects.
- 💸 Track reported cost and token usage by project in Usage & cost .
- ⏰ Schedule recurring work or launch tasks from GitHub and supported tracker events with Automations .
- 🌳 Agents can delegate independent work to child tasks, each in its own worktree, and receive their reports in the parent session.
- 🎫 Connect Jira or Linear to browse issues and launch tasks from your project tracker.
- 💾 No database. Everything is saved as plain files in .ai/cezar/ .

 Screenshots

 Parallel tasks — Run and queue many tasks, each in its own git worktree.

 

 Live run — Every step, tool call and token, as it happens.

 

 Variants — Run a task ×2 or ×3 and keep the best diff.

 

 Workflows — Build a task's pipeline as a node graph: agents, checks, loops, gates, PRs and CI, saved as YAML.

 

 GitHub — Hand an open issue to the agent in one click.

 

 Skills + Autonomous — Pick a playbook, flip Autonomous and walk away.

 

 Dashboard — See what needs your input or review, what is running and what finished across your workspace.

 

 Usage & cost — Compare reported spend and token usage across projects.

 

 Automations — Schedule maintenance and reviews, and see the week ahead alongside GitHub triggers.

 

 On your phone — the same cockpit, from the task list to the diff.

 
 
 
 
 
 
 

 Quick start

Two ways in: the desktop app for most people, or the npm package for servers and headless use.
Either way you need at least one agent CLI you're logged into (listed under npm / CLI).
The npm package also needs Node 20+ ; the desktop app uses yours, or downloads its own when you have none.

 Downloads

The desktop app (beta) runs the same local cockpit in its own window. It installs cezar on first launch,
keeps it up to date on the stable or nightly channel you pick in the cockpit, and switches between installed
versions from its menu.

To keep it installed, npm i -g @open-mercato/cezar puts cez and cezar on your PATH .

 Run it on a server

 

This sets up HTTPS, a login and a system service, so you can open the cockpit from anywhere, including your phone.
There are guides for Ubuntu VPS and macOS + ngrok.

 How it works

1. You describe a task. Type it, attach files, or start from a GitHub issue.
2. cezar runs a workflow (agent steps plus shell checks) in a new git worktree, using your agent CLI.
3. The cockpit streams every step live. If a check fails, the agent tries again and sees the error.
4. You check the result. Read the diff, send notes back, or open a draft PR.

install.title: Quick start
install.html:
Two ways in: the desktop app for most people, or the npm package for servers and headless use. Either way you need at least one agent CLI you're logged into (listed under npm / CLI). The npm package also needs Node 20+; the desktop app uses yours, or downloads its own when you have none.

Downloads

The desktop app (beta) runs the same local cockpit in its own window. It installs cezar on first launch, keeps it up to date on the stable or nightly channel you pick in the cockpit, and switches between installed versions from its menu.

Platform Download For
macOS Apple silicon (.dmg) Macs with an M-series chip
macOS Intel (.dmg) Macs with an Intel processor
Windows x64 installer (.exe) 64-bit Windows, setup installer
Linux AppImage Any 64-bit distribution, no install step
Debian, Ubuntu .deb package Debian, Ubuntu and derivatives (apt)
Arch, Omarchy, Manjaro .pkg.tar.zst Arch and Arch-based distributions (pacman)

All files: desktop-latest release. Windows release signing through SignPath.io (certificate by SignPath Foundation) is still being set up, so Windows SmartScreen may warn when you run the installer.

Homebrew (macOS)
brew trust --cask open-mercato/tap/cezar
brew install --cask open-mercato/tap/cezar

From desktop 0.1.12 on, the cask also puts the cez and cezar commands on your PATH. The app updates itself (auto_updates), so brew upgrade skips it unless you pass --greedy. Installed from the DMG instead? Get the same commands from the menu: Cezar → Install 'cez' command in PATH… (details).

npm / CLI

For servers, headless runs and anyone who lives in a terminal. You need Node 20+ and at least one agent CLI you're logged into: Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Cursor Agent, Google Antigravity CLI, Junie, Kimi Code, OMP, pi or Gemini CLI (needs an API key, Vertex AI or a Workspace licence — personal Google sign-in no longer works for it). git and gh are optional.

cd your-repo
npx cezar-run

This opens the cockpit at http://localhost:4321. If a compatible cockpit is already running, the command reuses it, adds the current project when needed, and opens that project's page instead of starting a duplicate server. Type a task, pick a workflow, then hit Start. npx cezar-cli still works too — it's the same package under its older name.

npx cezar-run run "add a --json flag to the export command"   # headless, no browser
npx cezar-run init                                            # scaffold .ai/cezar/
npx cezar-run@nightly                                         # try tonight's build

To keep it installed, npm i -g @open-mercato/cezar puts cez and cezar on your PATH.

Just want to look around? Run CEZ_DRY_RUN=1 npx cezar-run. It uses a built-in mock agent, so you don't need to log in.

Run it on a server
npx cezar-run server-install --platform ubuntu-vps

This sets up HTTPS, a login and a system service, so you can open the cockpit from anywhere, including your phone. There are guides for Ubuntu VPS and macOS + ngrok.
